title: Indian Travellers Increasingly Explore Homestays and Rental Properties
content:
Indian Travellers Increasingly Explore Homestays and Rental Properties

October 18, 2026

India's travel industry is witnessing a growing interest in homestays, holiday homes, serviced apartments and vacation rentals as travellers seek more space, flexibility and locally inspired experiences. Traditional hotels remain an important part of the hospitality sector, but alternative accommodation is becoming an increasingly popular option for families, groups of friends and business travellers.

A report titled How India Travels 2026 – The Homes Edit, released by Booking.com in collaboration with research firm VIDEC Consultants, highlights the expansion of India's alternative-accommodation market. According to the report, the segment's gross booking value is projected to reach ₹415 billion by the financial year 2029, reflecting changing travel preferences and growing demand for diverse accommodation options.

Alternative Accommodation Market Shows Strong Growth

The expansion of digital booking platforms has made it easier for travellers to discover and reserve properties beyond conventional hotels. Options now include independent homes, private villas, holiday cottages, serviced apartments and rooms offered by local hosts.

According to the Booking.com and VIDEC report, the number of digitally distributed alternative-accommodation listings in India increased from approximately 102,200 in FY2023 to 215,000 in FY2026. The growth indicates that more property owners are entering the market while online platforms are making these stays accessible to a wider audience.

Industry projections suggest that demand will continue to expand as domestic tourism, weekend travel and interest in lesser-known destinations create new opportunities for accommodation providers.

Why Travellers Are Choosing Homestays

One of the biggest attractions of homestays is the opportunity to experience a destination beyond its major tourist attractions. Staying in a local home can give visitors access to regional food, neighbourhood culture and recommendations from people familiar with the area.

Space and flexibility are also important considerations. Families may prefer properties with multiple bedrooms, kitchens and shared living areas, while groups can enjoy spending time together without booking several separate hotel rooms.

The Booking.com and VIDEC research found that 87% of surveyed travellers believed alternative accommodation could create more meaningful holiday memories. Around 85% associated these stays with authentic local experiences, while 83% highlighted their suitability for families and groups. Value for money was another important consideration for 83% of respondents.

However, the overall cost depends on the location, season, number of guests, cleaning charges and other fees. A homestay is not automatically cheaper than a hotel, so travellers should compare the total booking price before making a decision.

Smaller Cities and Emerging Destinations Gain Attention

The growth of alternative accommodation is extending beyond established tourism centres. Destinations such as Ayodhya, Indore, Greater Noida and Ghaziabad have recorded substantial increases in digitally listed alternative stays.

This expansion could create new opportunities for local entrepreneurs, homeowners and small tourism businesses. Visitors travelling to religious destinations, attending regional events or exploring less familiar locations may benefit from having more accommodation choices available.

The broader trend also reflects the growing role of domestic tourism in India's travel economy. A separate Oxford Economics report commissioned by Airbnb found that domestic travellers accounted for approximately 91% of Airbnb guests in India in 2024. The same report estimated that Airbnb-related activity contributed ₹113 billion to India's economy that year.

Business Travellers Also Explore Rental Properties

Alternative accommodation is no longer limited to holidays. Professionals travelling for extended assignments may prefer serviced apartments or rental properties that offer separate workspaces, additional living areas and facilities for longer stays.

These options can provide greater flexibility for people who need to work remotely while travelling. They may also suit colleagues travelling together or families accompanying someone on a business assignment.

As demand increases, accommodation providers face the challenge of maintaining consistent cleanliness, reliable check-in arrangements, accurate property descriptions and responsive customer support. These factors will be important in building traveller confidence and encouraging repeat bookings.

Challenges and the Road Ahead

Despite the market's growth, travellers should carefully review property photographs, guest feedback, cancellation policies, location details and additional charges before booking. Hosts, meanwhile, need to maintain appropriate safety standards and comply with relevant local regulations.

The future of India's alternative-accommodation sector will depend on balancing expansion with service quality. Digital platforms, better host training and improved property management could help strengthen the sector while creating opportunities for communities beyond major tourist destinations.

Conclusion

India's homestay and holiday-rental market is expanding as travellers seek greater space, flexibility and authentic local experiences beyond traditional hotels.

title: Airlines Tighten Cabin-Luggage Rules; Compact Trolleys Gain Attention
content:
Airlines Tighten Cabin-Luggage Rules; Compact Trolleys Gain Attention

October 18, 2026

Air travellers are paying closer attention to cabin-luggage size and weight limits as airlines enforce baggage requirements and passengers look for smaller, lighter trolley bags. Compact cabin suitcases are gaining attention among travellers who want to avoid last-minute repacking, additional charges and the inconvenience of having their luggage moved to the aircraft's cargo hold.

Although baggage allowances differ between airlines, routes, aircraft and ticket categories, many Indian domestic economy passengers are familiar with a cabin-baggage allowance of around 7 kilograms. Travellers are therefore increasingly considering suitcase dimensions and empty weight before making a purchase.

Airlines Follow Different Cabin-Baggage Limits

Airlines establish baggage rules to help ensure that luggage can be stored safely in overhead compartments or beneath passenger seats. However, the permitted dimensions and weight are not identical across carriers.

According to the published guidelines of IndiGo, passengers can carry one cabin bag weighing up to 7 kg, with maximum dimensions of 55 × 35 × 25 centimetres. Air India's economy and premium economy passengers are generally permitted one cabin bag weighing up to 7 kg, measuring no more than 55 × 40 × 20 centimetres.

These differences matter because a trolley that complies with one airline's requirements may exceed another airline's permitted dimensions. Handles, wheels and other external features must also be considered when measuring a suitcase.

Passengers should check the baggage policy associated with their particular booking before travelling, especially when their journey includes connecting flights operated by different airlines.

Why Compact Trolley Bags Are Attracting Attention

Compact trolley bags offer a practical option for short trips, business travel and weekend holidays. Their smaller dimensions can make them easier to manoeuvre through crowded terminals, while lightweight construction leaves more of the permitted baggage allowance available for clothing and other essentials.

Many modern cabin suitcases feature spinner wheels, telescopic handles, organised compartments and durable outer shells. Some models also include dedicated laptop compartments or external pockets that provide convenient access to travel documents and electronic devices.

However, travellers should avoid choosing a suitcase based only on a manufacturer's description such as “cabin size.” The actual external dimensions and empty weight are more important than the label.

A lightweight suitcase may be particularly useful when an airline imposes a strict weight limit. For example, a trolley weighing 2.5 kg leaves 4.5 kg for packed belongings under a 7 kg total allowance, assuming the airline's limit applies to the complete cabin bag.

What Travellers Should Check Before Buying

Travel experts generally recommend comparing three factors before purchasing a cabin trolley: dimensions, empty weight and durability.

First, passengers should measure the suitcase from its outermost points, including the wheels and handles. Second, they should check whether the packed bag will remain within the airline's weight allowance. Finally, they should consider wheel quality, handle strength, storage compartments and warranty coverage.

Travellers who frequently fly with different carriers may prefer a compact bag that fits within the strictest dimensions among the airlines they commonly use. Nevertheless, no suitcase can guarantee acceptance on every flight, since restrictions may vary by aircraft and booking conditions.

Passengers should also remember that cabin-baggage rules for personal items, laptops, power banks and other electronic equipment may differ. Spare lithium batteries and power banks, for example, are generally required to be carried in cabin baggage rather than checked luggage, subject to applicable airline and aviation-safety restrictions.

A Practical Shift Towards Smarter Packing

The growing interest in compact luggage reflects a broader emphasis on convenient and efficient travel. Instead of carrying oversized bags, many passengers are considering lighter suitcases, packing organisers and carefully planned essentials.

For short journeys, travelling with fewer belongings can reduce the effort involved in navigating airports and boarding flights. However, compact luggage is not always suitable for longer trips or passengers who need to carry specialist equipment, so the best choice depends on individual requirements.

Conclusion

Compact trolley bags are attracting attention as travellers prioritise lightweight designs, accurate dimensions and airline compliance to make flying more convenient.

title: Navratri 2026: Six Indian Cities for Garba and Dandiya Celebrations
content:
Navratri 2026: Six Indian Cities for Garba and Dandiya Celebrations

October 18, 2026

As the festive spirit of Sharadiya Navratri fills India, cities across the country are celebrating with traditional Garba, energetic Dandiya Raas, devotional music and colourful cultural events. The festival honours Goddess Durga and brings families, friends and communities together for nine nights of worship and celebration.

In 2026, Sharadiya Navratri began on October 11 and continues through October 19, followed by Vijayadashami on October 20. Gujarat remains a major destination for traditional Garba, while cities such as Mumbai and Delhi offer large-scale events that combine folk traditions with modern entertainment. Six cities stand out for visitors hoping to experience the festivities.

1. Vadodara, Gujarat: The Heart of Traditional Garba

Vadodara, also known as Baroda, is among India's best-known destinations for Navratri celebrations. The city is famous for its large Garba gatherings, traditional Gujarati music and community-led dance events.

During the festival, participants dress in colourful chaniya cholis, kediyus and other traditional outfits, joining dance circles that continue late into the evening. The city's celebrations offer visitors an opportunity to experience Garba as both a cultural tradition and an expression of devotion.

Travellers should check individual event schedules and entry requirements before attending popular venues.

2. Ahmedabad, Gujarat: Grand Celebrations and Cultural Performances

Ahmedabad attracts Garba enthusiasts with its large festival grounds, live folk music and organised Navratri events. The Vibrant Navratri Festival at GMDC Ground is a major attraction, bringing together traditional performances, devotional ceremonies, food stalls and cultural activities.

The city offers a range of experiences, from community gatherings to professionally organised events featuring prominent performers. Visitors can also explore Gujarati cuisine and local markets during the festive season.

For travellers seeking a large-scale celebration with traditional roots, Ahmedabad remains an appealing choice.

3. Rajkot, Gujarat: Community Spirit and Regional Traditions

Rajkot offers a distinctive Navratri experience shaped by local customs and community participation. Its Garba events provide an opportunity to enjoy Gujarati folk music, traditional dance movements and festive gatherings in a more community-oriented atmosphere.

Visitors can experience the warmth of local celebrations while exploring the region's food, handicrafts and cultural heritage. Those interested in traditional Garba rather than elaborate stage productions may find Rajkot particularly appealing.

4. Surat, Gujarat: Youthful Energy and Modern Festivities

Surat combines Gujarat's traditional Garba culture with a lively contemporary atmosphere. Its Navratri celebrations attract young people, families and groups of friends looking for energetic dance events and festive entertainment.

Many celebrations feature modern sound systems, organised dance spaces and a mix of traditional folk songs and contemporary music. Participants often prepare colourful outfits and attend events together, making the festival an important social occasion.

Surat is a strong option for visitors who want to experience both traditional dance and a modern festive environment.

5. Mumbai, Maharashtra: Garba Nights and Star Performances

Mumbai brings its own urban character to Navratri, with celebrations ranging from community-organised events to large ticketed Dandiya nights. Music performances, energetic dance floors and colourful traditional clothing contribute to the city's festive atmosphere.

The wider Mumbai metropolitan area, including Thane, also hosts popular celebrations. Visitors can choose between family-friendly gatherings and larger entertainment-focused events, depending on their preferences.

Because ticket prices, performers and venues vary, attendees should verify event details before making travel arrangements.

6. Delhi-NCR: A Diverse Mix of Garba and Dandiya Events

Delhi-NCR offers a wide selection of Navratri celebrations, attracting residents and visitors from different cultural backgrounds. Organised Garba and Dandiya nights take place at event grounds, community venues and cultural spaces across the region.

These events often combine traditional Gujarati music with DJs, stage performances, festive food and opportunities to dress in traditional attire. The variety makes Delhi-NCR a convenient option for people who want to enjoy Navratri without travelling to Gujarat.

Visitors should check event timings, ticket availability, transport arrangements and venue-specific rules in advance.

Tips for Enjoying Navratri 2026

People attending Garba and Dandiya events should wear comfortable clothing and footwear suitable for several hours of dancing. Staying hydrated, arranging safe transport and checking event entry rules can also make the experience more enjoyable.

As Navratri celebrations attract large crowds, booking tickets early where required and confirming venue details through official organisers are sensible precautions.

Conclusion

From Vadodara's traditional Garba to Mumbai's lively Dandiya nights, these six cities offer memorable ways to celebrate Navratri 2026 through devotion, dance and culture.

title: Nutrition Experts Discuss Food Choices That May Influence Sleep
content:
Nutrition Experts Discuss Food Choices That May Influence Sleep

October 18, 2026

Nutrition experts are highlighting the important connection between daily food choices and sleep quality, explaining that a balanced diet and appropriate meal timings may help people achieve more restful sleep. While no single food can guarantee a good night's rest, research suggests that dietary habits can influence how easily people fall asleep and how often they wake during the night.

How Diet Affects Sleep Quality

Sleep and nutrition are closely connected. The body requires a range of nutrients to support normal biological functions, including the processes that regulate sleep and wakefulness. Research suggests that diets rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, legumes, nuts and other nutrient-dense foods are associated with healthier sleep patterns.

According to the Sleep Foundation, diets containing adequate fibre and a variety of nutrients may support better sleep, while excessive added sugar and saturated fat have been associated with poorer sleep quality. However, individual responses can vary, and diet is only one of several factors affecting rest.

Foods That May Support Better Sleep

Experts recommend maintaining a balanced diet throughout the day rather than relying on a particular food immediately before bedtime. Foods containing tryptophan, magnesium and other essential nutrients may contribute to the body's normal sleep-related processes.

Milk, eggs, nuts, seeds, beans, bananas and whole grains can form part of a healthy eating pattern. Some research has also explored the potential sleep-related benefits of kiwi fruit, walnuts and tart cherries, although evidence for individual foods remains limited and further research is needed.

For people who feel hungry before bed, a light snack such as a banana with a small amount of nut butter, plain yoghurt with fruit, or whole-grain toast may be a reasonable option. The goal is to avoid going to bed uncomfortably hungry or overly full, rather than treating any snack as a guaranteed sleep remedy.

Caffeine and Alcohol May Disrupt Rest

One of the most important dietary considerations is caffeine consumption. Coffee, tea, energy drinks, cola and chocolate can contain caffeine, a stimulant that may delay sleep or reduce sleep quality. Its effects can last for several hours, and people who are sensitive to caffeine may need to avoid it from the afternoon onward.

Alcohol can also interfere with sleep. Although it may initially make someone feel drowsy, it can disrupt normal sleep patterns and contribute to waking during the night. Experts therefore advise against using alcohol as a way to fall asleep.

Large, fatty or spicy meals close to bedtime may cause indigestion or acid reflux, making it harder to rest comfortably. Eating dinner a few hours before sleeping and choosing lighter evening meals may help reduce these problems.

Healthy Habits Matter Alongside Food

Nutrition is only one part of good sleep hygiene. Maintaining a consistent bedtime, limiting screen exposure before sleep, exercising regularly and keeping the bedroom quiet, dark and comfortable can also support healthy sleep.

Experts caution against expecting dietary changes alone to resolve persistent insomnia or other sleep difficulties. People who regularly struggle to fall asleep, wake frequently during the night or feel excessively tired during the day should consider consulting a healthcare professional.

Conclusion

A balanced diet, limited late-day caffeine and lighter evening meals may support better sleep, but consistent routines and healthy lifestyle habits remain essential.

title: Experts Explain the Risks of a Blood Pressure Reading of 168/115
content:
Experts Explain the Risks of a Blood Pressure Reading of 168/115

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: A blood pressure reading of 168/115 mmHg is a serious health warning that should not be ignored. Medical experts advise people with readings this high to seek prompt medical assessment, even if they feel well. Although a single measurement cannot establish a diagnosis, the reading falls within the range of stage 2 hypertension under American Heart Association classifications and requires timely attention.

Blood pressure measures the force exerted by circulating blood against artery walls. The upper number, 168, represents systolic pressure when the heart beats, while the lower number, 115, represents diastolic pressure when the heart rests between beats. Both numbers are substantially above recommended levels.

Why Is 168/115 Blood Pressure Concerning?

Persistently elevated blood pressure places additional strain on the heart and blood vessels. Over time, this can damage organs and increase the risk of serious conditions, including heart disease, stroke, heart failure, kidney disease and vision problems.

The diastolic reading of 115 is particularly concerning because it indicates that pressure remains high even when the heart relaxes between beats. However, the overall risk depends on several factors, including a person's age, medical history, existing health conditions and whether the elevation is temporary or persistent.

High blood pressure is often called a silent condition because many people experience no obvious symptoms. Consequently, feeling normal does not mean that a reading of 168/115 can safely be ignored.

Is This a Hypertensive Crisis?

A reading of 168/115 is dangerously high, but it is below the commonly used threshold for a hypertensive crisis of approximately 180 systolic and/or 120 diastolic. Nevertheless, the lower number is close to that threshold, so prompt medical assessment is important.

If the reading is 180/120 or higher, repeat the measurement after at least one minute. If it remains that high, contact a healthcare professional immediately. If the elevated reading is accompanied by chest pain, difficulty breathing, sudden weakness or numbness, changes in vision, severe back pain or difficulty speaking, seek emergency medical assistance without delay. Do not wait for the blood pressure to fall on its own.

What Should You Do After a Reading of 168/115?

If you receive this reading, take the following steps:

  • Rest and recheck: Sit quietly for five minutes, keep your back supported and feet flat on the floor, and measure again using a properly fitted upper-arm cuff.

  • Seek prompt medical advice: If the reading remains around 168/115, contact a healthcare professional urgently today for assessment and advice.

  • Watch for warning signs: Chest pain, breathlessness, confusion, sudden weakness, speech difficulties or vision changes require emergency evaluation.

  • Take prescribed medicines as directed: Do not stop regular medication or take extra doses to lower your blood pressure without medical advice.

  • Avoid strenuous activity while seeking advice: Do not attempt to correct a very high reading through intense exercise or unproven home remedies.

A healthcare professional may review your medical history, repeat the measurements, assess possible causes and determine whether treatment needs to be started or adjusted.

Preventing Long-Term Complications

Long-term blood pressure control often involves medication, reducing salt intake, maintaining a balanced diet, exercising regularly when medically appropriate, avoiding tobacco and attending follow-up appointments. The right treatment plan varies between individuals.

People who have already been diagnosed with hypertension should monitor their readings as advised and take prescribed medication consistently. Regular monitoring helps healthcare professionals identify persistent elevations and adjust treatment when necessary.

Conclusion

A reading of 168/115 is dangerously high and needs prompt medical assessment. Recognising warning signs and obtaining timely treatment can help prevent serious complications.

title: Smriti Mandhana Shares Details of Her Early-Morning Workout Routine
content:
Smriti Mandhana Shares Details of Her Early-Morning Workout Routine

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: Indian cricketer Smriti Mandhana has offered insights into the disciplined fitness routine that helped shape her cricketing career. During a conversation with podcaster Raj Shamani, Mandhana revealed that she followed a demanding early-morning training schedule during her formative years, beginning at 5 a.m. Her routine combined yoga, high-intensity exercises and batting practice, highlighting the importance of consistency in developing professional sporting skills.

The details emerged during a recent podcast discussion in which the left-handed batter reflected on her early training, the influence of her mentor and the habits that contributed to her development as an international cricketer.

A 5 AM Start to the Day

Mandhana explained that her mentor, Amrita, introduced her to a strict fitness schedule when she was around 13 or 14 years old. The routine required her to wake up at 5 a.m. and complete a series of exercises before beginning her cricket-specific practice.

One of the first activities was performing 12 Surya Namaskars, a sequence of yoga movements commonly used to improve flexibility and mobility. She then moved on to short, intense exercise intervals designed to challenge her strength and endurance.

Her morning schedule demonstrates how structured physical preparation can become an important part of an athlete's development from a young age. Mandhana also credited her mentor with helping her develop discipline and the right approach to training.

Squat Jumps, Burpees and Mountain Climbers

Following the yoga sequence, Mandhana's routine included three demanding exercises: squat jumps, burpees and mountain climbers. Each exercise was performed for 30 seconds, and the sequence was repeated for five sets.

These movements target different aspects of physical conditioning. Squat jumps develop lower-body power, burpees combine strength and cardiovascular effort, while mountain climbers challenge core stability and endurance.

For a cricketer, physical conditioning can support quick movements on the field, running between wickets and maintaining energy throughout a match. However, Mandhana's account describes a routine from her formative years rather than a universal programme for every athlete. Training requirements vary according to age, fitness levels and individual needs.

Hours of Batting Practice

After completing her fitness exercises, Mandhana moved on to stationary shadow batting. She recalled practising the movements repeatedly until approximately 7:30 or 8 a.m.

Shadow batting allows players to rehearse their batting stance, footwork, balance and stroke movements without facing a bowler. Repeated practice can help players develop coordination and reinforce technical habits.

Mandhana said she followed this demanding schedule diligently for around five years. Her recollection highlights the amount of work that can take place away from stadiums and televised matches as young players develop their skills.

The routine also illustrates the combination of physical preparation and technical repetition required in cricket, where fitness alone cannot replace timing, concentration and sound batting technique.

Discipline Behind International Success

Mandhana's reflections highlight the influence of early coaching and consistent practice on her career. Her mentor helped her establish training habits and also encouraged her to think about leadership and the broader responsibilities associated with playing cricket.

Over the years, Mandhana has become one of India's prominent batters, recognised for her elegant stroke play and performances across international formats. Her experience offers young cricketers an example of how regular practice and a structured approach can support long-term development.

At the same time, effective training requires appropriate recovery, nutrition and professional guidance. Young athletes should adapt exercise routines to their individual abilities rather than copying an elite player's programme without supervision.

Conclusion

Smriti Mandhana's early-morning routine highlights how discipline, fitness exercises and consistent batting practice helped shape her development as an international cricketer.

Kangana Ranaut Combines Traditional Garba Style With Designer Fashion

Chhattisgarh, October 18, 2026: Bollywood actress and politician Kangana Ranaut has attracted attention with her vibrant traditional look for Navratri celebrations in Chhattisgarh. The actress shared photographs and behind-the-scenes videos of her festive appearance on social media on October 17, showcasing a designer lehenga-choli that combines Indian craftsmanship with contemporary fashion.

Kangana's outfit and styling reflect the growing popularity of traditional Indian clothing presented through modern designer aesthetics. Her appearance has also drawn attention to the importance of indigenous textiles and regional craftsmanship during India's festive season.

A Colourful Designer Lehenga-Choli

For the occasion, Kangana wore a richly decorated silk lehenga from the Indian designer label Torani. The outfit features a multicoloured design, intricate embroidery and decorative borders, creating a festive appearance suited to Navratri celebrations.

The ensemble includes a voluminous lehenga skirt paired with an embroidered choli and a matching dupatta. Tassel details and a lace-up back add a contemporary touch, while the traditional silhouette preserves the character of Indian festive attire.

According to Hindustan Times, the designer outfit is priced at approximately ₹2,10,500. Its combination of detailed craftsmanship and dramatic styling illustrates how luxury designers are reinterpreting traditional Indian clothing for modern celebrations.

Oxidised Silver Jewellery Completes the Look

Kangana complemented her outfit with statement oxidised silver jewellery. Her accessories included layered necklaces, broad arm cuffs, decorative rings and a circular maang tikka, creating a bold look inspired by traditional Indian adornment.

She styled her hair in a neat braid decorated with accessories and opted for winged eyeliner and understated lip colour. Small decorative details around her face added to the overall festive appearance.

The jewellery played an important role in balancing the elaborate outfit. Rather than relying exclusively on conventional gold accessories, the actress chose silver pieces that complemented the lehenga's colours and gave the ensemble a distinctive bohemian character.

Kangana Celebrates Indian Craftsmanship

Sharing moments from the photoshoot on Instagram, Kangana highlighted her appreciation for India's indigenous crafts and cultural heritage. She also extended Navratri wishes to her followers, describing the festival as a celebration of femininity and the divine feminine energy represented by Goddess Durga.

Her appearance in Chhattisgarh connected the fashion moment with the festive traditions associated with Garba. The traditional dance, particularly popular during Navratri, brings communities together through music, colourful clothing and energetic group performances.

Kangana's choice of designer wear demonstrates how contemporary fashion can draw inspiration from regional traditions while introducing new interpretations of familiar styles. Her emphasis on indigenous craftsmanship also reflects a wider interest in supporting and celebrating India's diverse textile heritage.

Traditional Fashion Meets Modern Trends

Garba fashion has evolved over the years, with designers experimenting with colour combinations, embroidery, mirror work, statement jewellery and contemporary blouse designs. Traditional chaniya cholis remain popular, but modern interpretations increasingly incorporate distinctive cuts, elaborate detailing and luxury fabrics.

Kangana's look fits into this broader trend, combining a traditional lehenga silhouette with dramatic accessories and designer embellishments. Her appearance may offer inspiration to fashion enthusiasts seeking festive outfits that preserve cultural elements while expressing individual style.

The look also highlights how celebrities can bring renewed attention to traditional Indian clothing through public appearances and social media. By choosing garments rooted in indigenous craftsmanship, they help keep conversations about Indian fashion traditions relevant to contemporary audiences.

Conclusion

Kangana Ranaut's vibrant Torani lehenga and oxidised silver jewellery showcase a modern interpretation of traditional Garba fashion, celebrating Indian craftsmanship and festive style.

title: Lakmé Fashion Week 2026 Showcases New Indian Fashion Trends
content:
Lakmé Fashion Week 2026 Showcases New Indian Fashion Trends

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: Lakmé Fashion Week x Fashion Design Council of India (FDCI) is showcasing the evolving landscape of Indian fashion, bringing together established designers, emerging talent and innovative collections. Running from October 13 to 18 at the Taj Palace in New Delhi, the six-day event highlights contemporary interpretations of traditional craftsmanship, modern occasionwear, sustainable design and changing fashion preferences.

Traditional Indian Craft Meets Contemporary Design

One of the key themes emerging from this year's fashion week is the combination of traditional Indian textiles with modern silhouettes. Designers are reinterpreting embroidery, handwoven fabrics and regional craft techniques to create clothing suited to contemporary lifestyles.

Collections presented during the event have explored ways to bring heritage-inspired elements into everyday clothing, formalwear and festive outfits. The emphasis on craftsmanship demonstrates how Indian designers are preserving traditional techniques while adapting them for changing consumer preferences.

Designer Pawan Sachdevaa's collection, RECAST, combines Indian craft traditions with contemporary tailoring. Techniques such as bandhani, shibori, kasuti and kantha appear alongside modern jackets, utility separates, relaxed trousers and structured outerwear. The collection uses fabrics including khadi, silk and denim to connect traditional craftsmanship with urban fashion.

Modern Bridal and Festive Fashion Takes Centre Stage

With India's festive and wedding seasons approaching, occasionwear remains an important focus of the event. Designers are presenting contemporary interpretations of bridal clothing, festive ensembles and formal outfits that balance traditional detailing with modern styling.

Designer Anushree Reddy showcased her bridal couture collection, MAYA, featuring intricate zardozi embroidery, sequins and glass-bead embellishments. Actress Sara Arjun appeared as the collection's showstopper, drawing attention to the combination of traditional bridal craftsmanship and contemporary design.

Designer Suneet Varma also presented creations inspired by Varanasi through his Kashi collection. The designs featured rich colours, elaborate embellishments and silhouettes such as draped sarees, dhoti skirts, jackets and lehengas. These collections reflect the continued popularity of culturally inspired clothing with updated cuts and styling.

Celebrity Appearances Add Glamour

Celebrity appearances have remained a major attraction at Lakmé Fashion Week 2026, bringing additional attention to designers and their collections.

Actors Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan served as showstoppers for Manish Malhotra's Luxury Prêt 2026 presentation on October 17. Khurrana wore an intricately embroidered black jacket, while Sara appeared in a sculpted black corset gown with a flowing skirt.

The collection explored contemporary occasionwear through detailed embellishments, relaxed tailoring and elongated silhouettes. Its palette included black, gold and silver, highlighting a modern approach to formal dressing. The showcase also introduced the designer's Men's Luxe Prêt line, reflecting growing interest in refined menswear and contemporary festive fashion.

Sustainability and Emerging Designers

Sustainability is another important element of this year's fashion week. The event's programme includes the R|Elan Circular Design Challenge, which highlights designers and innovators exploring more responsible approaches to fashion and material use.

The organisers have also provided platforms for emerging designers and students to present their work alongside established labels. These initiatives create opportunities for new talent to gain industry exposure and introduce fresh ideas to the fashion market.

Collaborations involving innovative textiles, traditional craft and contemporary sportswear demonstrate how designers are exploring alternatives to conventional fashion production. title: NLSIU Convocation Highlights Ethics and Integrity in the Legal Profession

NLSIU Convocation Highlights Ethics and Integrity in the Legal Profession

Bengaluru, October 18, 2026: The 34th annual convocation of the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, highlighted the importance of ethics, integrity and constitutional responsibility in the legal profession. Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant urged graduating students to uphold justice, defend individual liberty and remain committed to professional honesty as they begin their careers. The ceremony was held on October 17 and brought together graduates, university officials and distinguished guests.

CJI Surya Kant Emphasises Professional Integrity

Addressing the graduating students in his capacity as NLSIU Chancellor, Justice Surya Kant said that a successful legal career requires more than knowledge of statutes, regulations and judicial precedents. According to him, legal professionals must also possess the courage to defend what is right and the humility to listen to people whose voices are often overlooked.

He cautioned graduates against compromising their principles for convenience or choosing unethical shortcuts to achieve professional success. He encouraged them to preserve the values they had developed during their years at the university and apply those principles throughout their careers.

The Chief Justice stressed that integrity plays a crucial role in building professional credibility and maintaining public confidence in the justice system.

Fairness and Respect for Different Opinions

Another important theme of the address was the need to respect differing viewpoints. Justice Surya Kant encouraged graduates to listen before reaching conclusions, distinguish individuals from their opinions and disagree without undermining another person's dignity.

He described legal education as an experience that extends beyond textbooks and classroom learning. Law schools expose students to different ideas, beliefs and interpretations, helping them develop the intellectual independence necessary to examine complicated legal and social questions.

These qualities are particularly important for lawyers, judges and policymakers, whose decisions can affect individual rights, public institutions and society. By listening carefully and considering different perspectives, legal professionals can make more informed arguments and contribute to fairer outcomes.

The address reinforced the principle that disagreement should remain compatible with mutual respect and a commitment to justice.

Legal Profession as a Responsibility to Society

Justice Surya Kant described the legal profession as a responsibility that extends beyond personal achievement or financial success. He encouraged graduates to view their careers as opportunities to correct injustices, protect individual liberty and uphold the Constitution.

He also reminded them that legal professionals contribute to the justice system in several ways, including presenting arguments in court, drafting contracts, providing legal advice and interpreting the law. Each responsibility requires accuracy, fairness and an understanding of the consequences that professional decisions can have on people's lives.

His message underlined the importance of making ethical choices, particularly when professional pressures or personal interests create difficult situations. The Chief Justice encouraged graduates to remain guided by constitutional values and the principles of honesty they had learned during their education.

Graduates Celebrate Academic Achievements

The convocation also recognised the academic accomplishments of students completing their studies at NLSIU. A total of 330 students graduated from regular academic programmes, while another 1,390 students completed online and hybrid programmes.

The university awarded 50 gold medals to 24 graduates for outstanding performance across academic and co-curricular categories. Manhar Bansal was among the most notable award recipients, receiving 15 gold medals.

Padma Shri awardee and theatre personality Arundhati Nag attended the ceremony as chief guest. University Vice-Chancellor Professor Sudhir Krishnawamy presented the annual report for the 2025–26 academic year, outlining the institution's activities and achievements.

A Message for Future Legal Professionals

The ceremony served as a reminder that legal education carries responsibilities alongside academic recognition. Graduates entering litigation, corporate law, public policy, research and public service will be expected to apply their knowledge while maintaining ethical standards.

Justice Surya Kant's address placed particular emphasis on the connection between integrity and public trust. By remaining fair, respecting individual dignity and resisting unethical practices, young lawyers can help strengthen legal institutions and contribute to a more just society.

Conclusion

NLSIU's convocation highlighted honesty, fairness and constitutional responsibility, with CJI Surya Kant urging graduates to defend justice and reject unethical shortcuts.

title: Hollywood's portrayal of technology leaders is becoming more critical, reflecting growing public debate about AI, corporate power and accountability.
content:
Hollywood's Portrayal of Technology Leaders Draws Attention

Hollywood, October 18, 2026: Hollywood is increasingly turning its attention towards powerful technology leaders, with a new wave of films and documentaries examining the lives, influence and controversies surrounding some of Silicon Valley's most prominent figures. From social media executives to artificial intelligence pioneers, these productions reflect changing public attitudes towards the technology industry.

Recent projects focusing on figures such as Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, Sam Altman and Elizabeth Holmes have generated considerable discussion. Unlike earlier films that often highlighted the ambition and entrepreneurial spirit of technology founders, many of the latest productions take a more critical approach, exploring questions about corporate power, public accountability and the wider effects of technological innovation.

A Shift in Hollywood's Approach

One of the most notable examples is The Social Reckoning, the follow-up to the 2010 film The Social Network. The new production revisits issues surrounding Facebook, its leadership and the consequences of social media's growing influence. The story draws attention to concerns about digital platforms, corporate decision-making and the responsibilities of technology companies towards their users.

Another major project is Artificial, directed by Luca Guadagnino and featuring Andrew Garfield as OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman. The film examines events surrounding Altman's brief removal and subsequent return as OpenAI's chief executive in 2023. Its development has attracted attention because of the growing importance of artificial intelligence and the debate over how the technology should be developed and regulated.

Technology Leaders Become Subjects of Documentaries

Documentary filmmakers are also exploring the personal and professional lives of influential technology figures. Alex Gibney's documentary Musk examines Elon Musk's business empire, public influence and controversial decisions. Meanwhile, You Can See Everything focuses on Elizabeth Holmes, the former Theranos chief executive whose company became a major example of corporate fraud in the technology and healthcare sectors.

These projects demonstrate how technology leaders have become subjects of public fascination beyond business news and financial markets. Their decisions can affect millions of people through social media, artificial intelligence, digital communication and other widely used technologies.

However, such productions also raise questions about fairness and accuracy. Filmmakers must balance compelling storytelling with responsible portrayals of real people, particularly when dealing with disputed events or allegations. The individuals featured in these productions may also challenge the way their lives and decisions are presented on screen.

Growing Concerns About Technology and Artificial Intelligence

Hollywood's changing approach reflects broader concerns about the role of technology in everyday life. Artificial intelligence has created new opportunities in business, healthcare, education and entertainment, but it has also raised questions about employment, privacy, misinformation and the future of creative industries.

Technology companies are increasingly influential in shaping how people communicate, access information and consume entertainment. As a result, audiences are showing greater interest in stories that examine not only technological breakthroughs but also the responsibilities that accompany enormous financial and social power.

For Hollywood, these subjects provide opportunities to combine real-world events with compelling narratives. At the same time, the trend highlights the film industry's own complicated relationship with technology companies, which have become important investors, distributors and partners in entertainment.

A New Chapter in Technology Storytelling

The growing number of films about technology leaders suggests that Silicon Valley will remain an important subject for filmmakers. Future productions may explore the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence, competition between technology companies and the consequences of increasingly powerful digital platforms.

Whether these films lead to deeper public understanding will depend on how carefully they examine complex issues and distinguish documented facts from dramatic interpretation.

Conclusion

Hollywood's portrayal of technology leaders is becoming more critical, reflecting growing public debate about AI, corporate power and accountability.

title: Rajinikanth Pays Tribute to Music Composer Deva
content:
Rajinikanth Pays Tribute to Music Composer Deva

Chennai, October 18, 2026: Superstar Rajinikanth has paid an emotional tribute to veteran Tamil music composer Deva following his death at the age of 75 on October 17. Remembering their professional association and personal friendship, Rajinikanth described the composer as a kind-hearted individual known for his honesty, generosity and dedication to his family. Deva's passing has prompted an outpouring of grief across the Indian film industry, with actors, musicians and political leaders remembering his contribution to South Indian cinema.

Rajinikanth Remembers Their Musical Association

Rajinikanth and Deva shared a memorable professional relationship, collaborating on several successful Tamil films, including Annamalai (1992), Baashha (1995) and Arunachalam (1997). Their collaborations produced memorable songs and background music that became closely associated with the superstar's on-screen image.

One of Deva's most recognisable contributions was the signature musical theme accompanying Rajinikanth's title card. The composition became an iconic feature of the actor's film introductions and continued to resonate with audiences across generations.

In his tribute, Rajinikanth recalled the difficult conversation he had with Deva when he decided to work with A. R. Rahman on Padayappa. Despite having composed music for three successful Rajinikanth films, Deva reportedly responded graciously and encouraged the actor to collaborate with the younger composer. Rajinikanth remembered the incident as an example of Deva's generous character and lack of jealousy.

A Composer Known for His Humility

Beyond his professional achievements, Rajinikanth remembered Deva as a person who valued relationships and remained deeply connected to his family. The actor also spoke about the composer's challenging early years, when he worked hard to support his brothers before establishing himself in the film industry.

Deva's journey demonstrated how determination and musical talent could help an artist overcome difficulties and build a lasting career. Despite achieving considerable recognition, he maintained a reputation for warmth, simplicity and generosity.

Rajinikanth also recalled meeting Deva after one of his recent live concerts. The composer had reportedly expressed happiness at seeing younger audiences enjoying his music and hoped to continue performing for many more years. The memory made his sudden passing particularly painful for the superstar.

Deva's Lasting Contribution to Indian Cinema

Born Devanesan Chokkalingam, Deva was popularly known as Thenisai Thendral. During a career spanning nearly four decades, he composed music for more than 400 films across Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam cinema.

He made his Tamil film-composing debut with Mattukkara Mannaru in 1986 and subsequently became one of the industry's most recognisable music directors. His energetic compositions and memorable melodies helped bring Chennai's distinctive gaana musical tradition into mainstream Tamil cinema.

His work extended beyond film songs to background scores and compositions that became an important part of popular culture. Deva received several honours during his career, including the Kalaimamani award in recognition of his contribution to the arts.

Film Industry Mourns the Veteran Composer

Rajinikanth was among the prominent personalities who visited Deva's residence in Chennai to pay their final respects. Actor Kamal Haasan, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and several other film personalities also expressed their condolences.

The Tamil Nadu government announced that Deva would receive state honours, recognising his contribution to music and cinema. His death represents a significant loss for Tamil film music, but his songs and compositions are expected to remain popular with audiences for years to come.

Conclusion

Rajinikanth remembered Deva as a generous friend whose iconic music, humility and lasting contribution to Tamil cinema will never be forgotten.

The film witnessed an improvement in collections on its second day, attracting more viewers during Saturday screenings. According to early estimates, the movie earned approximately ₹5.50 crore in India net collections and ₹7.98 crore worldwide within its first two days. Directed by Avinash Arun and produced by Dinesh Vijan under the Maddock Films banner, Prahaar explores the challenges of criminal prosecution, courtroom proceedings and the pursuit of justice.

The story draws inspiration from the career of senior public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam, who became widely known for his role in several high-profile cases, including the prosecution of Ajmal Kasab following the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks.

For courtroom dramas, strong audience recommendations can help sustain theatrical business beyond the initial release period. Positive word of mouth, especially regarding the performances and central storyline, could encourage more people to watch the film.

Although the second-day improvement is encouraging, it remains too early to declare the film a commercial success. Its production budget, distribution costs and subsequent box-office performance must be considered before reaching a final verdict.

Rawalpindi, October 18, 2026: Pakistan's cricket team is facing growing pressure to end its long wait for an International Cricket Council (ICC) trophy, with next year's 2027 ODI World Cup emerging as a major target. Experienced batter Fakhar Zaman has acknowledged the expectations surrounding the team, saying players are determined to bring a major international title back to Pakistan.

Pakistan last won an ICC trophy in 2017, when it defeated India in the Champions Trophy final at The Oval in London. Since then, the team has experienced several disappointing campaigns, although it reached the final of the 2022 T20 World Cup before losing to England. The prolonged absence of major tournament success has increased expectations among supporters and former cricketers.

Fakhar Zaman recently admitted that the team's failure to win an ICC title for several years has become a significant source of pressure. He said the players have discussed the issue extensively and understand the disappointment experienced by supporters.

The 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup will be hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. The tournament represents an important opportunity for Pakistan to challenge for another major international title.

The team must also adapt to conditions in southern Africa, where pitches and weather can present different challenges. Building the right combination well before the tournament begins will be important for Pakistan's chances of progressing deep into the competition.

Pakistan's ongoing ODI tri-series against Sri Lanka and England is an important part of its preparations for the World Cup. The tournament, scheduled from October 18 to October 31, provides the team with an opportunity to test its combinations against quality international opposition.

Senior players, including Babar Azam, will be expected to make valuable contributions as Pakistan attempts to establish consistency in the 50-over format. The tri-series could help the management assess the team's strengths and identify areas requiring improvement before the global tournament.

Conclusion

Pakistan hopes to end its ICC trophy drought at the 2027 ODI World Cup, with Fakhar Zaman highlighting the pressure, preparation and expectations surrounding the team.

title: Anthropic Reports Changes in Workforce Experience and Meeting Time
content:
Anthropic Reports Changes in Workforce Experience and Meeting Time

San Francisco, October 18, 2026: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic has reported significant changes in its workforce structure, employee productivity and workplace routines as AI tools become increasingly integrated into daily operations. In a research report published on October 16, the company explained how its use of AI assistants and autonomous agents is changing hiring patterns, job responsibilities and collaboration among employees. The findings suggest that while AI is helping workers complete tasks more efficiently, it is also creating new responsibilities related to reviewing AI-generated work, managing automated systems and making strategic decisions.

According to Anthropic's report, the company has reduced the proportion of junior-level employees in its technical departments. The share of junior technical employees declined from 21% in early 2025 to 14%, while junior workers accounted for just 9% of new technical hires, compared with 27% previously. The company also reported that technical departments represented 56% of its workforce, down from 61% a year earlier. Anthropic said these changes reflect a combination of factors, including business expansion, changing hiring priorities and the growing ability of AI tools to help employees perform tasks that previously required specialised technical skills.

AI Agents Are Transforming Daily Work

Anthropic's research highlighted the rapid expansion of AI agents across its operations. These systems can perform tasks such as writing code, identifying software bugs, conducting tests, preparing documents and assisting with business processes. The company reported that, by August 2026, AI agents were working approximately six times as many hours as their human handlers when measured using the study's definition of agent operating time.

The increased use of AI has helped employees produce more code, close more sales per representative and process additional contracts. Workers are increasingly using AI assistants to automate repetitive tasks and focus on activities requiring human judgement, creativity and strategic thinking. However, Anthropic cautioned that producing more code does not automatically guarantee better software or improved business outcomes.

Meeting Time Increases Despite AI Adoption

One of the report's notable findings was that employees were spending more time in meetings despite the growing use of AI tools. According to internal calendar data, the median employee spent approximately 20% more time in meetings than a year earlier. Technical individual contributors also experienced a 16% increase in meeting time.

The company suggested that AI-driven productivity creates a greater need for human coordination, accountability and decision-making. As AI systems generate more information and complete more tasks independently, employees must review results, discuss priorities and coordinate complex projects. Consequently, time saved through automation does not always translate into fewer meetings or shorter working hours.

Human Skills Become More Important

Anthropic's findings indicate that hiring managers are increasingly prioritising candidates who demonstrate sound judgement, independence, adaptability and effective use of AI tools. Technical expertise remains important, but employers are placing greater emphasis on candidates' ability to work across different areas and supervise AI-assisted processes.

The research also highlights potential challenges for early-career professionals. If companies reduce entry-level recruitment because AI can handle more routine work, young workers may find fewer opportunities to gain practical experience. Employers may need to develop new training programmes that help junior employees build professional skills while working alongside AI systems.

Conclusion

Anthropic's report provides an important insight into how AI adoption can reshape workplace operations, recruitment and employee responsibilities. Although AI agents are helping the company increase productivity, the findings show that human judgement, collaboration and oversight remain essential. The experience may offer useful lessons for businesses considering wider AI adoption, although the results from one company should not automatically be treated as representative of the entire labour market.

title: Meta Updates Language Related to Web Scraping and AI Training
content:
Meta Updates Language Related to Web Scraping and AI Training

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: Meta Platforms has revised its commercial terms after concerns emerged that new language could allow the company to collect website content and use it for artificial intelligence (AI) training. The change follows criticism from journalists, publishers and legal experts who questioned whether the updated terms could give Meta broader permission to access online content, including news articles, without separate licensing agreements. Meta has clarified that the revisions do not change how its web crawlers operate and that website owners can continue using existing technical measures to communicate their preferences regarding automated access.

Why Did Meta Update Its Terms?

The controversy began after Meta introduced changes to its commercial terms for businesses using its platforms, including Facebook and Instagram. The proposed wording referred to automated tools such as web scrapers, bots and crawlers that could access, collect and analyse content from websites associated with businesses and their products or services. It also included language permitting the use of collected content to develop, improve, research and train Meta's products.

The wording raised concerns because news publishers and other businesses often maintain Facebook and Instagram accounts to promote their websites and reach audiences. Legal experts warned that the provision could potentially be interpreted more broadly than Meta intended, raising questions about copyright protection, content ownership and the use of online material to develop AI systems.

Meta Clarifies Its Position

Following the criticism, Meta removed the controversial reference to AI training from the relevant commercial terms and clarified that the provisions applied to its advertising and business products. The company stated that the changes were intended to consolidate existing language rather than introduce a new approach to web crawling.

Meta spokespersons also rejected suggestions that the company was attempting to bypass website restrictions or obtain unrestricted access to news content. According to the company, website owners can continue using the robots.txt protocol to communicate whether automated crawlers should access their websites. The clarification was intended to address concerns among publishers about the possible implications of the revised contractual language.

Impact on News Publishers and Website Owners

The development highlights the growing tension between technology companies developing AI systems and publishers seeking to protect their intellectual property. News organisations invest substantial resources in reporting, research, editing and producing original content. They are increasingly concerned that AI companies could use this material to improve their products without providing compensation or obtaining specific permission.

For website owners, the controversy underlines the importance of understanding the commercial terms of digital platforms and reviewing how automated systems access their content. Publishers can use technical controls, including robots.txt instructions, to communicate their preferences to compliant crawlers. However, the legal effectiveness of such measures can depend on the circumstances, the applicable terms and relevant copyright laws.

What Does This Mean for the AI Industry?

The dispute reflects a broader debate about how AI developers obtain training data and balance innovation with the rights of content creators. As companies invest heavily in generative AI, the demand for high-quality online information continues to grow. At the same time, publishers are exploring licensing agreements, legal remedies and technical restrictions to protect their work.

Clearer contractual language could help reduce confusion between technology companies and businesses that depend on digital platforms. Nevertheless, questions about copyright, data collection and compensation are likely to remain important as AI technology develops.

Conclusion

Meta's decision to revise its commercial terms demonstrates how concerns about AI training and website scraping can influence technology companies' policies. Although the company maintains that its crawling practices have not changed, the controversy highlights the need for greater transparency regarding how online content is accessed and used. The issue is likely to remain significant for publishers, website owners and AI developers as the industry continues to expand.

content:
Homegrown Smartphone Companies Enter the Budget Phone Market

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: India's budget smartphone market is witnessing renewed interest from domestic companies as rising memory chip prices and increasing production costs create opportunities for homegrown brands. Companies such as Lava, Ai+, Mivi and Boltt are looking to strengthen their presence in the affordable smartphone segment, particularly in devices priced below ₹20,000. Several established international manufacturers have reduced their focus on entry-level smartphones because higher component costs are putting pressure on profit margins. This shift is creating an opportunity for Indian companies to attract price-conscious consumers with affordable devices and locally developed products.

Indian Brands Target the Affordable Smartphone Segment

Domestic smartphone manufacturers are increasingly focusing on customers who want reliable devices at reasonable prices. Ai+, which operates under NxtQuantum Shift Technologies, has gained attention with its affordable smartphone offerings. Lava, an established Indian handset manufacturer, is also working to improve its product portfolio and expand its market presence. Meanwhile, electronics brands Mivi and Boltt are entering the smartphone business, seeking to build on their existing customer bases in the audio and wearable device markets. These companies are adopting competitive pricing strategies and online-first distribution models to reach customers without incurring the high costs associated with extensive traditional retail networks.

Rising Memory Chip Prices Create New Challenges

The growing cost of memory chips has become a major challenge for smartphone manufacturers worldwide. Memory components account for a substantial portion of the production cost of budget devices, leaving manufacturers with limited room to absorb further price increases. As a result, several established brands are prioritising higher-priced smartphones, where profit margins may be more attractive. This development is creating space for domestic manufacturers to compete in the entry-level market. However, Indian companies must carefully manage sourcing, manufacturing and distribution expenses to keep their products affordable while maintaining acceptable quality and performance.

Government Support for Indian Smartphone Brands

The Indian government is also encouraging domestic companies to develop their own smartphone brands through the ₹62,500-crore Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS). Notified in August 2026, the scheme aims to strengthen domestic manufacturing, encourage local research and development, increase component production and improve India's competitiveness in the global electronics industry. It includes incentives for Indian brands, with additional support for domestic design and research activities. The initiative is intended to help Indian companies move beyond assembling devices for international brands and develop products under their own names. It also aims to generate employment and increase the value created within India's electronics manufacturing ecosystem.

Competition With Global Smartphone Manufacturers

Despite the opportunities, homegrown companies face strong competition from established brands such as Xiaomi, Samsung, Vivo and Oppo. These companies have extensive distribution networks, strong brand recognition and considerable experience in smartphone development. Indian manufacturers will need to offer dependable hardware, regular software updates, attractive designs and reliable after-sales service to win consumer confidence. Competitive prices alone may not be sufficient to secure long-term success in a market where customers increasingly expect advanced cameras, powerful processors, long battery life and 5G connectivity.

Outlook for India's Smartphone Industry

The renewed entry of Indian brands could increase competition and provide consumers with more choices in the affordable smartphone segment. If domestic companies successfully improve their product quality and strengthen their supply chains, they could gradually capture a larger share of India's smartphone market. Government incentives and growing manufacturing capabilities may also support the development of locally designed devices.

Conclusion: The return of homegrown companies to India's budget smartphone market represents an important opportunity for the domestic electronics industry. Although rising component costs and competition from global manufacturers remain significant challenges, Indian brands could benefit from government support, cost-efficient distribution and increasing demand for affordable smartphones.

title: Starlink Says It Is Ready to Connect India With High-Speed Internet
content:
Starlink Says It Is Ready to Connect India With High-Speed Internet

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: SpaceX's satellite internet company Starlink has said it is ready to provide high-speed internet services across India, highlighting the company's preparations for entering one of the world's largest internet markets. Starlink said it has worked with Indian regulators, industry partners and telecom operators for more than five years and has built dedicated systems, gateways and other infrastructure within the country. The company said these preparations were made to ensure that Indian traffic can be handled safely and securely in accordance with local requirements.

Starlink's statement came after Reliance Industries said it welcomed competition in India's satellite communications sector, including competition from Starlink, provided that all companies comply with Indian laws and regulations. The exchange between the two companies comes amid increasing competition in India's emerging satellite broadband market. Reliance's Jio is also preparing to offer satellite internet services, while Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb is another major player seeking to launch commercial operations in the country.

Starlink has already made significant investments to prepare for its Indian operations. The company has established around 20 ground stations with hundreds of antennas and has designed its network to meet India's security and data-localisation requirements. Starlink executives have previously said that customer data would remain within India and that the company has been working with authorities to address regulatory and security requirements.

However, being prepared to launch does not necessarily mean Starlink can immediately begin commercial services. Satellite internet providers still need to complete the remaining regulatory process, including final security clearances and spectrum-related requirements. Starlink has obtained important licences and approvals, but the Indian government has maintained that all satellite operators must satisfy the same regulatory conditions before commercial operations can begin.

The issue has attracted considerable attention after Elon Musk publicly criticised delays surrounding Starlink's entry into India. Musk accused powerful business interests of attempting to prevent Starlink from entering the market, although the Indian government rejected suggestions that the approval process was biased or discriminatory. Officials have said that Starlink, Jio's satellite business and Bharti-backed OneWeb are subject to the same regulatory framework and security requirements.

India represents an important opportunity for satellite broadband because millions of people, particularly in rural and remote areas, still have limited access to reliable high-speed internet. Satellite technology can potentially provide connectivity in locations where traditional fibre networks and mobile towers are difficult or expensive to deploy. This could make Starlink particularly relevant for remote communities, businesses, educational institutions and emergency communication services.

Price will also be an important factor in determining Starlink's success. Elon Musk has indicated that the service would need to be affordable for Indian consumers, where mobile data prices are among the lowest globally. Starlink will therefore face a significant challenge in competing with established operators such as Jio and Airtel, which already have extensive terrestrial networks and large customer bases.

The growing competition could ultimately benefit Indian consumers by increasing the number of connectivity options available in the country. Satellite broadband could complement existing fibre and mobile networks rather than directly replacing them, particularly in areas where conventional infrastructure is difficult to establish.

Conclusion: Starlink's declaration that it is ready to connect India marks another important development in the country's satellite internet race. While the company has built much of the required infrastructure, final regulatory and spectrum-related steps remain important before commercial services can begin. If approved, Starlink's entry could increase competition, improve connectivity in underserved areas and accelerate India's satellite communications industry.

title: Indian Markets Face Pressure From Inflation and Oil Prices
content:
Indian Markets Face Pressure From Inflation and Oil Prices

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: Indian stock markets are facing significant pressure as rising inflation, elevated crude oil prices and continued foreign investor outflows weigh on market sentiment. The benchmark BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty 50 have experienced volatility as investors assess the impact of higher energy costs on India's economic growth and corporate earnings. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have pushed international crude oil prices higher, increasing concerns about India's import bill and inflation outlook. Market participants are also closely monitoring interest-rate decisions by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and global economic developments that could influence investment flows.

Rising Inflation Raises Economic Concerns

Inflation has emerged as a major concern for India's economy. According to data released on October 12, India's retail inflation increased to 5.54% in September 2026, compared with 4.83% in August. Rising food prices contributed significantly to the increase, with food inflation reaching 7.74%. Higher prices for essential commodities can reduce household purchasing power and affect consumer spending. If inflation remains elevated, businesses may also face higher operating costs, potentially affecting profitability and future investment decisions.

Crude Oil Prices Put Pressure on Indian Markets

Higher crude oil prices are another major factor influencing investor sentiment. India imports a substantial proportion of its crude oil requirements, making its economy vulnerable to fluctuations in international energy markets. On October 14, Brent crude prices reached approximately $106 per barrel amid escalating geopolitical tensions and concerns about disruptions to oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Expensive oil increases India's import expenditure and can put pressure on the rupee. It can also raise transportation, manufacturing and logistics costs, affecting companies across several industries.

Sensex and Nifty Remain Under Pressure

Indian equity benchmarks have struggled to maintain a sustained recovery amid these economic challenges. On October 14, the Nifty 50 declined 0.44% to close at 22,622.70, while the Sensex fell 0.34% to 72,781.89. Selling pressure affected several sectors as investors reassessed corporate earnings prospects and the potential impact of higher oil prices. Although some technology stocks attracted buying interest following positive earnings developments, broader market sentiment remained cautious. Investors are expected to remain selective until there is greater clarity on inflation, energy prices and global financial conditions.

Foreign Investor Outflows Add to Market Volatility

Foreign portfolio investor selling has added another challenge for Indian equities. Higher global interest rates and uncertainty surrounding international markets have encouraged some investors to reduce exposure to emerging economies. Persistent foreign fund outflows can weaken demand for Indian shares and increase volatility. A weaker rupee can further complicate the situation by making imported goods, particularly crude oil, more expensive. Domestic institutional investors may provide some support, but a sustained market recovery will depend partly on improving global conditions and renewed foreign investment interest.

Outlook for the Indian Stock Market

The near-term outlook for Indian markets will depend on several important factors, including crude oil prices, inflation data, RBI policy decisions, corporate earnings and foreign investment flows. A decline in energy prices could ease inflationary pressure and improve business sentiment. Conversely, continued geopolitical tensions and persistently high oil prices could put further pressure on company margins and household spending.

Conclusion: India's stock market faces a challenging environment as inflation, expensive crude oil and foreign investor outflows create uncertainty. Although the country's underlying economic activity remains an important source of support, investors are likely to remain cautious until inflationary pressures ease and global conditions become more favourable.
