title: Indian IT Companies Report Strong AI-Related Revenue Trends
content:
Indian IT Companies Report Strong AI-Related Revenue Trends

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: India's leading information technology (IT) companies are reporting significant growth in artificial intelligence (AI)-related business as global enterprises increasingly invest in automation, generative AI, cloud computing and intelligent software solutions. Major IT service providers, including Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), HCLTech, Wipro and Tech Mahindra, are expanding their AI capabilities to meet rising demand from international clients. However, despite the rapid expansion of AI-related services, overall revenue growth across the industry remains uneven because of cautious client spending and pressure on traditional technology services.

TCS Reports Strong Growth in AI Business

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), one of India's largest IT services companies, has reported strong momentum in its artificial intelligence business. During the September quarter of fiscal year 2026–27, the company's annualised AI revenue exceeded $3.1 billion, representing sequential growth of approximately 19.2%. This performance highlights the increasing importance of AI-powered solutions in the company's business strategy. TCS is helping businesses implement generative AI, automate operations, modernise software systems and improve productivity. Nevertheless, the company's overall revenue growth remains comparatively modest, demonstrating that the expansion of AI services does not necessarily translate into equally strong growth across its entire business.

HCLTech Sees Rising Demand for Advanced AI Solutions

HCLTech has also reported encouraging results from its AI-related operations. The company recorded annualised advanced AI revenue of $876 million in the September quarter, increasing 78% year-on-year in constant-currency terms. Its overall revenue reached approximately $3.7 billion, while new deal bookings totalled $3.3 billion. The company attributed its performance to growing client demand, stronger deal activity and expanding adoption of AI-powered technology services. HCLTech is investing in advanced AI capabilities to help enterprises improve business processes, develop intelligent applications and accelerate digital transformation. These developments indicate that specialised AI services are becoming an increasingly important source of business opportunities for Indian technology companies.

Wipro and Other IT Firms Adapt to the AI Revolution

Wipro is also strengthening its AI-focused business strategy as companies seek technology partners capable of delivering intelligent automation and digital transformation. The company is developing AI-native solutions and expanding its services to help customers integrate AI into their operations. However, its latest quarterly results indicate that the broader business environment remains challenging. Wipro's IT services revenue increased only 0.6% year-on-year in constant-currency terms during the September quarter, while its total bookings declined sequentially. This contrast highlights the difficulty of converting growing interest in AI into sustained revenue growth. Tech Mahindra has also reported improving consolidated revenue, reflecting differing growth patterns among India's major technology companies.

AI Creates New Opportunities and Challenges

The growing adoption of artificial intelligence is creating opportunities in software development, cybersecurity, data analytics, cloud services and enterprise automation. Businesses are increasingly seeking AI solutions that can reduce operating costs, improve decision-making and enhance customer experiences. Indian IT companies are well positioned to support these transformations because of their established client relationships and large technology workforces.

However, AI adoption also presents challenges for traditional IT service providers. Automation can reduce the time and labour required to complete certain projects, potentially lowering the fees companies receive for conventional technology services. IT firms must therefore develop new AI-based offerings while ensuring that productivity improvements translate into additional business, stronger margins or improved profitability. Industry experts believe that the long-term impact will depend on whether AI creates new technology spending or primarily changes how existing budgets are allocated.

Outlook for India's IT Industry

The outlook for India's IT sector will depend on global technology spending, enterprise investment decisions and the speed at which AI projects move from experimental stages to large-scale implementation. Companies that successfully combine artificial intelligence with consulting, cloud computing and digital transformation services could gain a competitive advantage. At the same time, slower client spending and pricing pressure may continue to affect traditional IT operations.

Conclusion: Strong AI-related revenue trends demonstrate that artificial intelligence is becoming a major growth opportunity for India's IT industry. Although companies such as TCS and HCLTech are reporting substantial increases in AI business, sustained industry growth will depend on their ability to turn technological demand into new contracts, recognised revenue and long-term profitability.

title: India Restricts Sugar Diversion for Ethanol Production in 2026–27
content:
India Restricts Sugar Diversion for Ethanol Production in 2026–27

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: The Indian government has restricted the use of sugarcane-based products for ethanol production during the 2026–27 ethanol supply year to protect domestic sugar supplies and control rising prices. According to a new tender issued on October 16, oil marketing companies will not procure ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup or B-heavy molasses during the upcoming supply year, which begins on November 1, 2026. However, ethanol produced from C-heavy molasses will remain eligible. The decision comes amid concerns about lower sugar production, adverse weather conditions and increasing prices in the domestic market.

Why Has the Government Restricted Sugar Diversion?

India has experienced growing concerns over sugar availability following weaker-than-expected production and unfavourable weather conditions in major sugarcane-producing states, particularly Maharashtra and Karnataka. Reduced rainfall has raised concerns about sugarcane yields, while increased demand during the festive season has added pressure to domestic supplies. Retail sugar prices have also risen significantly, prompting the government to prioritise the availability of sugar for household consumption and food-related industries. By restricting the use of sugar-rich raw materials for ethanol, the government aims to retain more sugar within the domestic market.

Impact on the Ethanol Industry

The new policy represents a significant change for sugar mills that previously diverted sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses towards ethanol production. These feedstocks contain recoverable sugar that can otherwise be used for food consumption. Under the revised procurement policy, ethanol producers will need to rely more heavily on alternative raw materials, including maize, broken rice and surplus rice procured through the Food Corporation of India. This shift could increase competition for grain-based feedstocks and influence production costs across the ethanol industry.

India's 20% Ethanol Blending Target

Despite restricting sugar-based ethanol, India intends to continue its nationwide E20 programme, which aims to blend 20% ethanol with petrol. The programme is designed to reduce dependence on imported crude oil, improve energy security and support the use of alternative fuels. To maintain ethanol supplies under the new restrictions, oil marketing companies have invited bids for approximately 11 billion litres of ethanol made from eligible feedstocks. The government will therefore need to balance its energy objectives with the need to maintain adequate domestic sugar availability.

What Does the Decision Mean for Consumers and Farmers?

The restriction could help improve sugar availability and ease price pressures if domestic production remains below expectations. Consumers and food-processing businesses may benefit from improved supplies, although the actual impact on retail prices will depend on production levels, demand, imports and government market interventions. For sugar mills, the policy could change the balance between selling sugar directly and producing ethanol. While mills may lose some opportunities in sugar-based ethanol production, higher sugar prices could support revenue from sugar sales. However, the effects will differ across companies depending on their production capacity and feedstock arrangements.

Outlook for India's Sugar and Ethanol Markets

India's sugar and ethanol industries will closely monitor weather conditions, sugarcane yields, government procurement policies and grain prices during the 2026–27 season. The revised policy highlights the challenge of balancing food security with the country's transition towards cleaner fuels. The government will need to ensure that alternative feedstocks can meet ethanol demand without creating excessive pressure on grain supplies.

Conclusion: India's decision to restrict sugar diversion for ethanol production reflects its immediate priority of protecting domestic sugar availability amid production concerns and rising prices. At the same time, greater reliance on grain-based ethanol is expected to play an important role in maintaining the country's fuel-blending programme.

title: BEML Secures a ₹5,400 Crore Bullet Train Order
content:
BEML Secures a ₹5,400 Crore Bullet Train Order

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML), a government-owned engineering and manufacturing company, has secured an order worth more than ₹5,400 crore from the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) for India's ambitious Mumbai–Ahmedabad bullet train project. Announced on September 18, 2026, the contract covers the supply and maintenance of high-speed trainsets and related works for the 508-kilometre high-speed rail corridor. The order represents a major milestone for India's railway manufacturing industry and highlights the country's efforts to strengthen domestic capabilities in advanced transportation technology.

Major Boost for India's Railway Manufacturing

Under the contract, BEML is expected to manufacture 16 additional high-speed trainsets for the Mumbai–Ahmedabad corridor. These trains will be supplied alongside two B28 trainsets that the company is already developing in collaboration with Integral Coach Factory (ICF), Chennai. The new order is expected to strengthen BEML's position in the railway sector and expand its contribution to India's high-speed rail infrastructure. The design and manufacturing of these trains will also provide opportunities to develop domestic engineering expertise and reduce dependence on imported rolling stock.

India's Indigenous Bullet Train Programme

BEML is developing India's domestically manufactured B28 bullet train at its Aditya High-Speed Rail Complex in Bengaluru. The train has a design speed of 280 kilometres per hour and an intended operational speed of 250 kilometres per hour. The first two trainsets are being developed under an earlier contract worth approximately ₹866.9 crore. The Railways has set an ambitious target for introducing the domestically manufactured trains on an initial section of the Mumbai–Ahmedabad corridor, although testing, certification and other operational requirements must be completed before passenger services begin.

Mumbai–Ahmedabad Bullet Train Project

The 508-kilometre Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor is India's first major bullet train project. It is designed to connect important economic centres across Maharashtra, Gujarat and the surrounding region, including Mumbai, Surat, Vadodara and Ahmedabad. The project aims to reduce travel times, improve passenger comfort and strengthen connectivity between major commercial hubs. Once operational, the corridor is expected to support business travel, tourism and regional economic development. However, construction, infrastructure integration and safety testing remain important factors in determining when services can begin.

Financial and Industrial Impact

The ₹5,400 crore order is significant for BEML because it adds a substantial project to the company's existing order book. It could support future revenue, manufacturing activity and employment opportunities across the railway supply chain. The contract may also create business opportunities for component manufacturers, technology providers and other domestic suppliers involved in high-speed train production.

The development comes as India continues to invest in modern railway infrastructure and explore additional high-speed rail corridors. BEML's experience in manufacturing these trainsets could help strengthen the country's long-term capabilities in railway engineering. However, the financial benefits will depend on successful execution, production schedules, cost management and timely delivery.

Conclusion

BEML's ₹5,400 crore bullet train order marks an important step in India's efforts to develop domestic high-speed rail technology. The contract strengthens the company's role in the Mumbai–Ahmedabad project and supports the broader goal of modernising the country's railway network. As manufacturing and infrastructure development progress, the project will remain an important indicator of India's ambitions in high-speed transportation.

title: Indian Rupee Extends Its Winning Streak Against the US Dollar
content:
Indian Rupee Extends Its Winning Streak Against the US Dollar

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: The Indian rupee continued its upward momentum against the US dollar, recording six consecutive sessions of gains and posting its strongest weekly performance in seven months. On October 16, the rupee closed at ₹94.92 per US dollar, gaining seven paise during the trading session. The recovery followed a period of significant pressure on the Indian currency, which had approached record lows in recent weeks. Measures introduced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), along with a weaker US dollar and easing crude oil prices, helped support the domestic currency.

RBI Measures Support the Rupee

The Reserve Bank of India has introduced several measures to reduce pressure on the rupee and improve stability in the foreign exchange market. These steps include redirecting some dollar purchases by state-owned oil companies away from the spot market and tightening rules governing foreign exchange derivative positions. The central bank has also increased the cost of certain transactions that allow market participants to bet against the rupee. These measures have helped reduce speculative dollar demand and encouraged traders to unwind positions taken in anticipation of further weakness in the Indian currency.

Weaker US Dollar Provides Additional Support

The decline in the US dollar's strength has also contributed to the rupee's recovery. Changes in US Treasury yields and expectations regarding the Federal Reserve's future interest-rate decisions have influenced international currency markets. When the dollar weakens against other major currencies, emerging-market currencies such as the Indian rupee can receive additional support. Improved sentiment in Indian equity markets has also contributed to the recent recovery, although foreign investment flows and global economic uncertainty remain important factors for investors to monitor.

Crude Oil Prices Remain a Key Concern

Despite the recent gains, elevated crude oil prices continue to pose a challenge for the Indian economy. India imports a substantial portion of its crude oil requirements, and higher international prices increase the country's import bill and demand for US dollars. This can put renewed pressure on the rupee and affect India's trade balance. Geopolitical tensions in West Asia and uncertainties surrounding global energy supplies could also influence oil prices in the coming weeks. A sustained decline in crude oil prices would help reduce import costs and could provide further support to the Indian currency.

What the Rupee's Recovery Means for India

A stronger rupee can benefit Indian businesses that import crude oil, electronics, machinery and other products priced in dollars. It may also help moderate imported inflation by reducing the domestic cost of foreign goods. However, exporters could face challenges because a stronger rupee makes Indian products relatively more expensive for overseas buyers when prices are expressed in foreign currencies. The overall economic impact will depend on how long the currency's recovery lasts and how exchange-rate movements affect different industries.

Outlook for the Indian Currency

Market participants are expected to closely monitor RBI policy decisions, crude oil prices, foreign investment flows and developments in the US economy. Although the rupee's six-session winning streak has improved short-term market sentiment, analysts caution that a lasting recovery will require stronger underlying economic conditions. Persistent demand for dollars, foreign portfolio outflows and a widening trade deficit could limit further gains.


Conclusion: The Indian rupee's recent rally represents a significant reversal after weeks of pressure. RBI measures and favourable global developments have helped strengthen the currency, but maintaining this momentum will depend on oil prices, capital flows and broader economic conditions.

title: Fairfax Financial Set to Acquire a Majority Stake in IDBI Bank
content:
Fairfax Financial Set to Acquire a Majority Stake in IDBI Bank

New Delhi, October 18, 2026: Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings is set to acquire a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank for approximately ₹52,878 crore ($5.56 billion), marking a landmark development in India's banking sector. On October 14, the Union Cabinet approved Fairfax as the strategic buyer for the proposed transaction. The deal is expected to become one of the largest foreign investments in India's financial services industry and represents a significant step forward in the government's banking privatisation programme.

The transaction involves the sale of a 30.48% stake held by the Government of India and a 30.24% stake owned by the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC). Fairfax's acquisition will give the Canadian financial services company a controlling interest in the bank, subject to the completion of regulatory requirements. Following the transaction, the government is expected to retain a 15% stake, while LIC will hold approximately 19% of IDBI Bank.

Fairfax Plans to Expand Its Financial Services Business

Fairfax Financial Holdings, led by Indian-born Canadian businessman Prem Watsa, has established investments across several financial services businesses. The acquisition of IDBI Bank offers the company an opportunity to strengthen its presence in India's expanding banking and financial markets.

According to Fairfax's announcement, the company also plans to contribute its existing Indian financial investments, including Digit Insurance and IIFL Capital, to IDBI Bank, subject to regulatory approvals. If implemented, the proposal could expand the bank's business beyond traditional banking into insurance, investment banking and wealth management. The proposed restructuring may also create opportunities to develop a broader financial services platform for individual and corporate customers.

IDBI Bank's Financial Recovery

IDBI Bank has made considerable progress in improving its financial health over recent years. The bank previously faced significant challenges from bad loans, with its gross non-performing asset ratio reaching approximately 31.78% in September 2018. Government support, improved recovery efforts and tighter risk management helped reduce the ratio to around 2.32% by March 2026.

This improvement has made the bank a more attractive investment opportunity. With more than 2,000 branches and a substantial customer base, IDBI Bank provides Fairfax with an established presence in India's competitive banking market. The new ownership could bring additional investment, management expertise and opportunities to improve digital banking services, although the actual impact will depend on the company's future strategy.

Impact on India's Banking Sector

The proposed acquisition is an important milestone in India's efforts to attract foreign investment and reduce government ownership in financial institutions. The government expects the transaction to generate significant proceeds while allowing the bank to pursue its future growth under a new controlling shareholder.

However, the deal also presents challenges. Fairfax will need to comply with the Reserve Bank of India's regulatory requirements, including the assessment of its suitability to control the bank. The transaction must also satisfy other applicable conditions before completion.

Conclusion

Fairfax Financial's proposed acquisition of a majority stake in IDBI Bank could reshape the bank's ownership structure and strengthen its position in India's financial services industry. The deal highlights growing international interest in India's banking market and the government's commitment to strategic disinvestment. Investors, customers and industry experts will closely monitor the transaction as it progresses towards completion.

title: India–US Trade Deal: First Phase Nears Completion
content: NEW DELHI, Oct 15 (Reuters) - The first phase of an India-US trade deal is in the final stages of drafting, India's trade minister said on Thursday, but reiterated that ​New Delhi would proceed only if it secures an advantage over competing exporters. New Delhi ‌and Washington agreed to a framework for the deal in February which brought down to 18% from 50% the punitive tariff on most Indian goods imposed in August last year after a previous round of talks ​collapsed. Since then, negotiations have run into hurdles, with officials on both sides signalling that efforts ​to reach a final agreement have slowed. Indian trade minister Piyush Goyal said the "first ⁠tranche" of the deal would be finalised soon. "It's going through the final contours, the legal ​drafting, and we hope to be able to finalise that soon and operationalise that once we ​get comparable advantage or competitive advantage over our peer countries," a statement from his office quoted him as saying at an event in New Delhi. Goyal was referring to New Delhi's efforts to secure a tariff advantage for ​Indian exporters over competing economies such as Bangladesh, Vietnam and Indonesia in the US market. India ​wants to ensure its exporters face tariffs no higher than those imposed on competing economies. Trade Secretary Rajesh Agrawal ‌echoed Goyal's ⁠comments. "We anticipate concluding and signing the trade deal at the earliest possible time," Agrawal said, adding that India was seeking preferential market access and greater tariff stability under the proposed agreement. India's goods exports to the United States rose to $42.79 billion in April-August from $40.39 billion a year earlier. In ​the fiscal year 2025/26, ​India recorded a ⁠trade surplus of nearly $34 billion with the United States. Neither side has publicly detailed the reasons for the delay, but one recent complication has been ​a new US law that could pave the way for tariffs of ​up to ⁠100% on Indian goods because of New Delhi's continued purchases of Russian oil. The trade talks have unfolded against a backdrop of increasingly strained ties between India and the United States, complicating efforts to steady ⁠their ​trade partnership. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will visit India and ​Uzbekistan, from October 17 to 22, and will meet government and business leaders to discuss energy cooperation, commercial investment and ​broader economic ties.
